scope: Engineering value and task-role triage of the remaining R5 inventory only. No formal evidence grade, admission score, implementation approval, new registry entry, benchmark reproduction, pretrained asset download or Stable promotion.

items.name: Z-GCNETs
items.canonical_title: Z-GCNETs: Time Zigzags at Graph Convolutional Networks for Time Series Forecasting
items.task_role: Topology-enhanced graph forecasting with precomputed zigzag persistence images
items.incremental_value: Adds evolving topological summaries beyond local graph convolution or continuous graph dynamics; this is not another ordinary adjacency filter.
items.rationale: The graph backbone is only one part of the method. Faithful forecasting depends on zigzag persistence features, their time-window provenance and node/time alignment. Official preprocessing uses Gudhi, Dionysus, Ripser and Persim; silently substituting generic graph features would lose the contribution.
items.reopen_when: A caller-owned topology-feature contract, leakage-safe offline generation and bounded dependency-free model core are specified and shown useful against existing graph peers.
items.code_license: MIT root code license inspected; dataset and generated topology assets need separate provenance.
notes: Pinned root and model README require precomputed zigzag-persistence images for train/validation/test.
A topology pipeline is not supplied by the current dense forecasting batch.
No local author-benchmark reproduction or topology runtime measurement.

items.name: STSGCN
items.canonical_title: Spatial-Temporal Synchronous Graph Convolutional Networks: A New Framework for Spatial-Temporal Network Data Forecasting
items.task_role: Supervised localized synchronous space-time graph forecaster
items.incremental_value: Joint graph convolution over neighboring time slices differs from separated temporal/spatial operators, though the existing fusion-graph family already covers related goals.
items.rationale: Primary identity and official implementation are available, but the complete pinned source tree exposes no LICENSE, COPYING or NOTICE. Public code is not a permission grant. No implementation or score is assigned while this gate remains unknown.
items.reopen_when: An explicit applicable author source license or independently cleared implementation becomes available, then demonstrate meaningful incremental utility against STGCN and STFGNN.
items.code_license: Unknown; no explicit grant found in the complete inspected tree.
notes: R5 source/permission hold retained, not converted into low-value rejection.
STSGCN and STGCN are different paper identities.

items.name: DA-RNN
items.canonical_title: A Dual-Stage Attention-Based Recurrent Neural Network for Time Series Prediction
items.task_role: Historical-driving-series input attention plus recurrent temporal-attention prediction
items.incremental_value: Provides a compact dual input/temporal attention formulation for exogenous driving sequences, unlike TFT's richer variable selection or TimeXer's patch-based exogenous fusion.
items.rationale: The report explicitly links a community implementation, not the original authors' release. Its complete pinned tree has no explicit license. A faithful interface must distinguish past driving variables from target history and not assume future drivers are known.
items.reopen_when: Resolve implementation provenance/permission and the target-versus-exogenous single/multihorizon contract; then test whether it fills a practical gap beyond current exogenous models.
items.code_license: Unknown for the report-linked community code; no LICENSE/COPYING/NOTICE found.
notes: Do not label KurochkinAlexey/DA-RNN an official author repository.
Other TensorFlow/PyTorch community ports are not automatically cleared substitutes.

items.name: DeepGLO
items.canonical_title: Think Globally, Act Locally: A Deep Neural Network Approach to High-Dimensional Time Series Forecasting
items.task_role: Global temporal matrix factorization regularized by a TCN plus local TCN forecasting
items.incremental_value: Explicit global low-rank temporal factors plus local convolutional correction complement graph-factor and recurrent global forecasting approaches.
items.rationale: The global latent factors are tied to a fitted collection of series and time positions, with alternating optimization and later forecasting. Treating this as an ordinary independently sampled sliding-window forward would omit the method's main global component.
items.reopen_when: Define a global fit/forecast lifecycle, collection identity, rolling-origin refitting and persisted factor state without changing the common model/runner boundary implicitly.
items.code_license: BSD-3-Clause text verified in license.txt; GitHub metadata NOASSERTION is not the actual license conclusion.
notes: Official environment assumes CUDA and includes scientific/data packages; a native port is not a turnkey wrapper.
This is a real forecasting model; current task-contract mismatch is not low scientific value.

items.name: DeepState
items.canonical_title: Deep State Space Models for Time Series Forecasting
items.task_role: RNN-conditioned linear Gaussian state-space probabilistic forecasting with Kalman inference
items.incremental_value: Adds explicit seasonal/level/trend state-space structure and analytical filtering/likelihood under globally shared recurrent parameterization, rather than autoregressive output sampling or a variational latent Transformer.
items.rationale: This is a genuine missing probabilistic mechanism with mature licensed reference code and no required pretrained weights. The MXNet implementation still needs a full native contract for seasonal indicators, known covariates, missing observations, posterior conditioning and joint-path sampling.
items.reopen_when: Complete formal six-gate admission and honest scoring, audit independent experiment provenance, and design/tests for Kalman covariance stability, observed masks, covariate timing, correlated samples and persistence before implementation.
items.code_license: Apache-2.0 LICENSE and NOTICE inspected; source remains an MXNet reference, not a native torch_like implementation.
notes: Pinned src/gluonts/mx/model/deepstate/_network.py conditions the RNN on time/static features; observed targets update the LDS posterior, not ordinary target autoregression.
Original paper Table2/3 does not support a universal-best claim; the small-data advantage is regime-dependent.

Cross-sectional State-Space Forecasting with Partial Pooling (https://sangrey.io/cross_sectional_forecasting_with_partial_pooling.pdf) reports new DeepState experiments but shares the original authors' institution; full independence/protocol grading remains open.
N-BEATS AppendixC.5 uses published DeepState values and cannot count as an independent rerun.
No formal evidence grade, score, implementation approval or benchmark promotion is assigned here.

items.name: STRIPE
items.canonical_title: Probabilistic Time Series Forecasting with Shape and Temporal Diversity
items.task_role: Diversity-oriented probabilistic forecasting framework with shape/time DPP sampling objectives
items.incremental_value: Targets diversity across plausible future shapes and timing, whereas diffusion or variational latent probabilistic forecasts do not automatically optimize these explicit structured diversity objectives.
items.rationale: Its forecast quality/diversity depends on the generator and structured DPP/shape-time learning or selection protocol, not merely a renamed deterministic head. Official pinned source has no explicit license grant; output distribution, sampling and training interfaces still need specification.
items.reopen_when: Resolve source permission and define the complete generator/diversity objective and sampling contract with proper scoring and diversity evaluation; do not equate diverse samples with calibrated uncertainty.
items.code_license: Unknown; complete pinned tree has no LICENSE/COPYING/NOTICE.
notes: Canonical title omits the report's extra word Structured.
No neural or probabilistic wrapper is implemented in this review.

items.name: ST-MetaNet
items.canonical_title: Urban Traffic Prediction from Spatio-Temporal Data Using Deep Meta Learning
items.task_role: Geographical-attribute-conditioned meta graph-attention and recurrent traffic forecaster
items.incremental_value: Generates location-specific graph/recurrent behavior from geographical node/edge attributes, unlike learned node-adaptive convolution or supplied-embedding graph attention.
items.rationale: The capability is real, but current graph coverage is already broad and there is no concrete geographic-metadata use case. Porting old MXNet/DGL machinery plus a rich node/edge-attribute contract has lower present general-library payoff than filling missing probabilistic capabilities.
items.reopen_when: A real traffic application supplies geographical node/edge metadata and demonstrates a useful gap against AGCRN/GMAN under a matched protocol; then revisit the native meta-parameter mechanism.
items.code_license: MIT, copyright2019ZheyiPan; official source LICENSE text inspected.
notes: Report-linked lucktroy/ST-MetaNet is a fork; parent panzheyi/ST-MetaNet was separately resolved and pinned.
Official flow example uses 989-dimensional node features and32-dimensional edge features; these numbers are an example, not universal mandatory dimensions.
Skip is a present scope/maintenance judgment, not proof of inferiority or duplication.

items.name: TRMF
items.canonical_title: Temporal Regularized Matrix Factorization for High-Dimensional Time Series Prediction
items.task_role: Classical global temporal matrix factorization with fitted autoregressive latent dynamics
items.incremental_value: Handles global low-rank structure and missing entries with temporal regularization; neither existing peer is an interchangeable implementation of this optimization algorithm.
items.rationale: TRMF is a valid forecasting algorithm, but it needs collection-level factor fitting/alternating optimization, not an nn.Module window forecaster. The repository's classical namespace discovers real sklearn estimators; it is not an implicit authorization to add a new classical fitting system.
items.reopen_when: Classical/global-fit forecasting is explicitly scoped with collection identity, optimization/state serialization and leakage-safe refitting; separately verify exact implementation provenance and license.
items.code_license: No original implementation license verified in this audit; report/community pointers are not assumed author clearance.
notes: Author homepage code lead could not be retrieved; this is an audit limitation, not proof that original code does not exist.
Out of the current neural-backbone queue does not mean not a model.

items.name: DSARF
items.canonical_title: Deep Switching Auto-Regressive Factorization: Application to Time Series Forecasting
items.task_role: Switching deep latent autoregressive factorization with a Markovian regime prior
items.incremental_value: Adds discrete recurring regimes and switching nonlinear latent dynamics beyond a continuous variational latent forecast or a learned linear-dynamics framework.
items.rationale: A meaningful switching-state capability exists, but the official complete source tree has no explicit license. Variational posterior state, lag selection, sequence-level fit and forecast/sample semantics need more than a dense one-shot prediction wrapper.
items.reopen_when: Obtain clear source permission and specify faithful regime inference, lagged latent likelihood, sequence fitting and uncertainty tests; evaluate a genuinely multimodal or switching use case.
items.code_license: Unknown; complete pinned source tree has no LICENSE/COPYING/NOTICE.
notes: Report narrative/table inconsistencies and dataset-count wording are not copied as universal superiority.
No separate state-estimation or switching-training subsystem is added.

items.name: ST-Norm
items.canonical_title: ST-Norm: Spatial and Temporal Normalization for Multi-variate Time Series Forecasting
items.task_role: Spatial/temporal normalization modules applied to existing forecasting backbones
items.incremental_value: Explicitly separates temporal high-frequency and spatial local components; this differs from the existing graph backbone and de-stationary attention but can be composed as normalization machinery.
items.rationale: The primary contribution is two reusable normalization modules that can augment WaveNet/Transformer-style forecasters. A new backbone registration would conflate the component with its host model. Source permission is additionally unknown in the complete pinned tree.
items.reopen_when: A reusable normalization-layer integration is explicitly scoped and licensed reference permission is resolved; test axes, training/eval statistics and comparison to existing normalization without inventing a new model identity.
items.code_license: Unknown; no LICENSE/COPYING/NOTICE found in the complete pinned tree.

The paper explicitly presents modules that integrate into canonical architectures; this is not a low-quality judgment.

items.name: CoST
items.canonical_title: CoST: Contrastive Learning of Disentangled Seasonal-Trend Representations for Time Series Forecasting
items.task_role: Self-supervised seasonal/trend representation learning followed by downstream regression
items.incremental_value: Disentangles seasonal/trend representations using time/frequency contrastive objectives rather than only decomposing a supervised forecasting backbone.
items.rationale: The actual workflow learns representations first and fits a downstream regressor. Calling an encoder plus arbitrary forecast head CoST would omit the contrastive and downstream-fit contribution; the library should not silently absorb an SSL training platform.
items.reopen_when: Representation-pretraining and downstream-estimator composition is explicitly requested, with training-only representation fitting, saved encoder/regressor ownership and temporal leakage tests.
items.code_license: BSD-3-Clause LICENSE.txt inspected; official repository is archived.
notes: Canonical paper describes the two-stage contrastive representation plus regression workflow.
No extra backbone count is created for a training paradigm.

items.task_role: Frozen pretrained language-model reprogramming framework for forecasting

items.name: xLSTM-Mixer
items.canonical_title: xLSTM-Mixer: Multivariate Time Series Forecasting by Mixing via Scalar Memories
items.task_role: Supervised scalar-memory recurrent mixing architecture
items.incremental_value: Stable gated scalar-memory refinement, joint temporal-variate recurrent mixing and dual-view reconciliation extend existing MLP mixing.
items.rationale: Authentic exponential sLSTM gates and states require native numerical and gradient parity. Upstream uses xlstm 1.0.3 and Lightning; its CUDA sLSTM path requires compute capability at least 8.0. Published efficiency cannot be assumed for a portable rewrite.

items.name: SKOLR
items.canonical_title: SKOLR: Structured Koopman Operator Linear RNN for Time-Series Forecasting
items.task_role: Supervised FFT-gated spectral branches, measurement MLPs and structured linear-RNN forecasting architecture
items.incremental_value: Learned soft spectral selection and explicit branch-specific linear recurrence differ from current framework-oriented Koopa's GRU and operator and FiLM's fixed Legendre memory.
items.rationale: Downgraded from initial review_next to hold after deeper evidence. A bounded native architectural difference remains, but useful benefit over current peers is unproven; independent TimeES runs report SKOLR worse than Koopa in all 16 ETT settings. The official runner imports absent modules and forces CUDA, its parallel variant contains breakpoints, and root MIT does not override NC helper headers. These burdens no longer justify immediate admission work.
items.reopen_when: Pinned core and license audit, native recurrence and spectral parity, stability and gradient tests, and independently run controlled experimental comparisons satisfy governance evidence requirements.
items.code_license: Pinned root MIT for native core; utils/losses.py, utils/m4_summary.py and data_provider/m4.py retain explicit Element AI CC BY-NC 4.0 and patent-reservation headers
notes: Initial review_next priority superseded by deeper source and independent experimental evidence; no formal score or implementation approval.
Pinned core is layers/KoopBlock.py, blob 4d5823543d2878dad4711fded20a7ca595a22427; scripts select KoopBlock, not a model called SKOLR.
Appendix C.2 claims branch parallelism, while scripted KoopBlock core uses branch and time loops; KoopBlock_P is unfinished.
Report results use horizons 48,96,144,192 and lookback twice horizon; do not compare directly with standard long horizons.

Independent experiments: https://arxiv.org/html/2609.32384v2 Appendix C.5 Table 9; vendorized core, experiment adapter and five-seed ETTh1 script audited at wwy155/TimeES commit cdb476741c3b32f76c9474d7351a524b68bee7bf. Exact result logs and full-grid tuning provenance not established.
Independent TimeES ETTh1 script uses global mask and CI=false, unlike official ETTh2 CI=true/channel-mask script; not an exact original-protocol replication.
Separate independent energy experiment: https://www.mdpi.com/1996-1073/19/18/4289; claimed same-condition runs on Spain and Panama, source ZIP present but not inspected.
Avoid all NC M4/loss helpers and do not vendor the broken training harness.

No independently rerun external comparison was identified in this audit; official five-seed claims do not create independent evidence.
Pinned loader passes first-forecast phase but model gathers seq_len cyclic templates from that phase; do not silently reinterpret it as history-start phase.
Source normalization uses default sample variance and attached statistics; seq_len1 and gradient semantics need explicit native policy.
With only primary and official evidence, C ceiling is 75 before risks, never core80.
